back: A failure likely to pass on its own. A retry may succeed, so the harness retries it with a limit.
A failure that repeats on every try. The harness does not retry it: it fixes the request, or stops.
A wait that doubles after each failed try, up to a cap.
Clients that failed together would retry together. A random part of the wait spreads their retries out.
After a set number of failures in a row, it opens and holds calls back for a cooldown, so retries stop adding load.
front: What does a circuit breaker do?

back: A limit on the retries a run or client may make, so retries cannot grow without end.
A value sent with a request, so a repeated request is recognised and not run twice.
